question_text: Distinguish between a ligament and a tendon.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Ligament
steps.why: The two structures differ in what they join and in whether elastic fibres are present, so both facts are written for each one.
common_mistakes: Writing that a ligament joins muscle to bone. That is a tendon.
Saying a ligament has only elastic fibres. Collagen is the main fibre in both.
steps.memory_tip: Ligament: bone to bone. Tendon: muscle to bone. Say the pair together, never one alone.
steps.margin_note: What it joins, and what it is made of. Two lines.
lines: A ligament connects one bone to another bone.
It is made of collagen fibres with a few
elastic fibres, so it can stretch a little.

steps.label: Tendon
steps.why: A tendon must not stretch, because the pull of the muscle has to reach the bone unchanged, and that is why it carries no elastic fibres.
common_mistakes: Giving both the same fibres. A ligament has some elastic fibres; a tendon has collagen only.
steps.memory_tip: A tendon is tight: collagen only, no stretch, so the muscle's pull reaches the bone.
steps.margin_note: State the contrast in one boxed line, then give the tendon's own two facts.

insider_note: Both marks turn on four words — bone to bone, muscle to bone; the fibre difference is what separates a full answer from a half one.
